contribution.position: I hold my earlier position. I am answering qa's claim on axis:risk that error_rate is 0.4%, comfortably inside the 1% budget, per artifact:perf-report. That does not match the artifact. artifact:perf-report records error_rate at 3.4% at peak load against a 1% budget, and the 0.4% figure appears in no listed artifact. Until qa names the run or condition that produced 0.4%, such as a non-peak run or a different build, it cannot offset the peak-load measurement. Ops' point (axis:operability) that artifact:ops-runbook documents deploy and rollback steps is true and is new context for me. But rollback limits how long a failure lasts. It does not lower the error rate, and it does not show that retries behave safely at 3.4%. artifact:incident-log shows two sev2 incidents from retry storms, which is the failure mode an elevated refresh error rate at peak would trigger. artifact:test-report (412 passed, 0 failed) covers functional behavior, not load. Evidence gap: no listed artifact shows the retry or backoff behavior of this change under load, and none shows a re-measured peak error rate. Either would change my view.
